summary:
Cosmic Whispers is a web-based platform that makes it easier to explore and understand observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission. The project uses actual SPHEREx data collected at different times and compares the images to find regions where changes or unusual patterns may be present.

We developed a system that processes and aligns astronomical images, creates difference maps, and highlights possible candidate regions for further study. It also includes an interactive 3D star environment, clickable objects, observation images, graphs, and information panels so users can explore the data themselves.

The main aim is to make astronomical data easier to understand instead of limiting it to complex scientific files. This project can help students, space enthusiasts, and researchers explore changes in the sky and develop a better understanding of how repeated observations help scientists study the universe.
details:
How does it work?

We used actual SPHEREx observation data collected at different times. First, we processed and aligned the images so that they could be compared properly. We then created difference images and maps to identify regions showing unusual patterns or changes. These regions are displayed as possible candidates for further investigation.

The website also includes a rotating 3D star environment, clickable objects, observation images, graphs, and information panels. Users can explore different parts of the project and view the results in an interactive way.

Benefits and intended impact

One of the main benefits is that users do not need to work directly with complicated astronomical data files to understand the observations. The website presents the results visually and makes them easier to explore. It can be useful for students, astronomy enthusiasts, and anyone interested in space research.

We hope this project encourages more people to explore real space data and understand how comparing observations over time can help scientists study changes in the universe.

Tools and technologies used

  • Python for coding and data processing.
  • Google Colab for development and testing.
  • Astropy for handling astronomical FITS files.
  • NumPy and Pandas for calculations and data analysis.
  • Gradio for building the web application.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the website interface.
  • Three.js for the rotating 3D star environment.
  • Plotly for interactive graphs.
  • Google Drive for storing project files.
  • GitHub and Render for deployment.

What makes our project creative?

We wanted to do more than just display astronomical images and tables. So, we designed a space-themed interface where users can explore a rotating starfield, click on objects, view observations, and understand the changes shown by the data. The combination of actual scientific observations and an interactive visual experience makes the project different from a regular data analysis tool.

Factors we considered

While developing the project, we focused on using genuine NASA data, making image comparisons as accurate as possible, keeping the website easy to use, and presenting the results in a clear way. We also made sure to treat the detected regions as candidates for further study rather than confirmed discoveries.

Our aim is to make exploring the universe a little easier and more interesting for everyone.
dataRefs: SPHEREx Public Data Archive – NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA)
